---
applyTo: "Dockerfile,.dockerignore,.volcengine/**,.github/workflows/test.yml,.github/workflows/test-docker.yml,.github/workflows/deploy-main.yml"
---

Keep the workspace image based on Ubuntu 26.04 and build it for Linux amd64, the supported Linux architecture of the bundled Lynx runtime. Read Node and Rust versions from `.nvmrc` and `rust-toolchain.toml`, and keep the Corepack version aligned with `.github/actions/pnpm-install/action.yml`.

The public CP build has timed out connecting to both Ubuntu archive and security hosts over IPv4 as well as failing IPv6 connections; forcing IPv4 alone does not fix that failure. Pass `UBUNTU_MIRROR=http://mirrors.volces.com/ubuntu` as a build argument in CP, and apply the optional override to both stages' `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources`. Leave Ubuntu's default sources in place when the argument is unset. Preserve suites, components, and the Ubuntu signing keyring. Use `apt-get update --error-on=any` so a failed index download reports the actual network error instead of continuing to misleading package-not-found errors. CP's `buildkit-custom@3.0.0` ignores `--platform` in `buildParams`; use its default single-architecture Linux amd64 build and pass `--target runtime` there.

Build npm workspaces through the repository-root Turbo command used by `deploy-main.yml`, excluding both `benchx_cli` and `@lynx-js/benchmark-*`. Keep Wasm packages in this build. Exclude `swc_plugin_reactlynx`, `swc_plugin_reactlynx_compat`, and `web-core` only from the subsequent native Cargo build, and enable `ui_judge/server` to include its optional binary and packaged runtime assets.

Use separate builder and runtime stages. Keep only Node, production workspace dependencies, package outputs, and final native deliverables in the runtime image. Reinstall production dependencies with `--prefer-offline --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` after removing workspace `node_modules`; do not rely on `pnpm prune` to prune a monorepo. Avoid `--offline`: a previous full install does not guarantee every package snapshot remains available for the production reinstall, so missing snapshots must be allowed to download. Preserve source files exported by workspace packages. Remove Cargo targets, build caches, and generated source maps before copying the workspace into the runtime stage. Copy both Rust executables, the React transform shared library, the generated launcher, the Lynx runtime library, and `lynx_core.js` explicitly. Strip only binaries built here, preserving the downloaded Lynx runtime unchanged. Do not copy compiler toolchains, package managers, headers, or download caches into the final image. Use BuildKit cache export `mode=min` so CI builds do not export intermediate builder layers.

Set runtime `LYNX_LIB_PATH` and `LYNX_CORE_JS_PATH` to the copied assets. The headless runner otherwise retains Cargo-injected paths into the SDK cache removed during cleanup.

Export production `node_modules` directories into a separate tree while preserving their workspace-relative paths and symlinks. Keep downloaded Lynx SDK files separate from Rust outputs. Use independent `COPY --link` layers for Node, production dependencies, the SDK, workspace files, and compiled Rust deliverables. Remove pnpm installation bookkeeping with variable timestamps and normalize exported timestamps, including symlinks, so unchanged file contents can produce reusable layers across commits. Do not remove source files used by package exports. Dependency splitting must preserve Node resolution through both pnpm links and workspace links. Exclude `.volcengine` from the runtime filesystem.

Do not copy host `node_modules`, Cargo targets, Turbo caches, or local environment files into the Docker build context. Validate the complete Dockerfile in the independent `test-docker.yml` workflow only for pull requests changing `.github/workflows/**`. Start without depending on the Ubuntu build, and keep Docker validation out of `test.yml` and its `done.needs`. Do not add push or merge-group triggers that would run this expensive build unconditionally. In GitHub Actions, build without pushing images, registry credentials, or `packages: write` permission. Do not build Docker images in `deploy-main.yml`. Pin Docker Actions to verified commit SHAs.

Keep Volcengine publishing separate in `.volcengine/pipeline.yaml`. Use the documented CP YAML 2.0.0 structure with `agentPool: public/prod-v2-public`, `resourcesPolicy: none`, and the required `buildkit-custom@3.0.0` component to build and push the root Dockerfile's `runtime` stage for Linux amd64. Bash steps may anonymously clone `main`, read its full commit hash, and clean their workspace files, but must not build with Docker CLI or require a Docker daemon or Buildx in the public pool. Configure a generic Webhook as a start signal without branch or commit parameters; ignore its payload. Do not bind a GitHub code source. The console schema currently accepts only its enumerated preset component values; do not insert a made-up or placeholder custom component reference. Use `exec@1.0.0` for Bash commands.

The public CP pool's Git has rejected `git clone --no-tags`. Use `--depth=1 --single-branch --branch main` without `--no-tags` for the anonymous checkout. Keep the clone command, including its `source` destination argument, on one line when copying it into CP. A detached `source` token invokes Bash's builtin instead of naming the checkout directory.

Keep checkout limited to cloning main and recording HEAD. Let Git, BuildKit, and the publishing command report their own errors instead of adding file-existence checks, duplicate credential checks, or a regex check of Git's commit output. Retain checks that protect destructive image cleanup, including digest verification before deletion.

Use the cloned full commit hash as the final image tag. CP rejects arbitrary outputs on `exec@1.0.0`: task outputs must reference outputs already defined by the component. Writing `/tekton/results/commitSha_main-head` cannot add that output to the preset component. Do not assume a shell export persists into another component or that an image-address input executes shell commands. Keep checkout, build, tagging, and cleanup in one task so they share the workspace. Save the cloned HEAD in a file; never resolve main again after the build.

BuildKit pushes a temporary tag using `PIPELINERUN_ID`. Use `custom-image@2.0.0` with the official Alpine regctl image and `.volcengine/publish-image.sh` to publish the saved HEAD. Pin the source by digest and verify the destination digest before cleanup. Preserve an existing commit tag rather than replacing its image on retries. Keep the newest ten commit images by image configuration creation time, not lexical SHA order, plus the current commit and protected images. `CR_PROTECTED_COMMITS` protects space-separated deployed and rollback SHAs; non-SHA tags also protect their digests and corresponding SHA tags. Only SHA tags and the reserved `build-*` temporary tags are cleanup candidates. Other runs' temporary tags must be older than 24 hours before cleanup. Serialize publishers for the same repository using the platform's concurrency controls.

Inventory all tags and their digests before cleanup. Protect both retained root manifests and their index descendants. Use `regctl tag delete` only for temporary aliases sharing a retained digest. Delete an obsolete manifest by digest only if no retained tag or index references it; never delete blobs or recursively delete child manifests. Registry garbage collection controls when unused storage is reclaimed. Do not swallow inventory, publication, or deletion failures. Configure CR retention separately for interrupted runs and orphaned data, since pipeline cleanup only runs after a completed build. Do not export the BuildKit temporary image address as the final task artifact. Print the final address and digest in the tagging step log.

Configure BuildKit CR authentication using the console-generated `loginCredential` structure; do not invent its nested schema or commit credentials. Command steps also need CR username/password environment variables provisioned in the platform, with the password kept private. Disable shell tracing, pass the password through stdin, and remove the temporary regctl configuration on exit. Keep the full cloned repository as the build context, enable component-managed caching independently of runtime image cleanup, and remove the checkout and commit file after success. The image defaults to `/bin/bash`, so service deployments must override the startup command for the selected application. Local YAML and shell checks do not replace CP execution with the actual CR permissions.
